name: Haiku macro/sector rotation
strategy: Position for the 2026 macro backdrop centered on the AI and semiconductor super-cycle. Overweight semiconductor infrastructure (NVDA, TSM, AMD, ASML) at the core of AI capex, combined with AI-beneficiary mega-cap software and cloud (MSFT, GOOG, AAPL) plus growth (TSLA), with defensive diversification (UNH, COST) for risk management. Equal-weight across 10 positions to capture macro rotation into AI-driven capex cycle.

orders.reason: Down 16% in H1, underperforming S&P 500 despite AI narrative; cloud software is secondary to semiconductor hardware in the core super-cycle.
Negative H1 return (-10%); not aligned with AI infrastructure semiconductor thesis.
Weakest performer in current book at +7.6%; defensive lagged H1 and not core to AI/semiconductor infrastructure.
Memory chip leader with +187% in H1; extraordinary demand validates AI infrastructure buildout and memory super-cycle continuation.
Optical/photonics up +95% in H1; critical enabler for AI data center connectivity and infrastructure deployment.
Semiconductor equipment manufacturer; complements ASML positioning to capture chip manufacturing equipment demand from H2 super-cycle.

outlook: The AI and semiconductor super-cycle should accelerate in H2 2026; H1 data confirms memory and optical interconnect are the strongest secular tailwinds. Direct chip makers and equipment suppliers are positioned to capture outsized value.
